Didymoteicho Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Didymoteicho, Greece

Not demolished. A predominantly Sephardi Jewish community existed in Didymoteicho from the early Ottoman period (14th century), numbering a few dozen families by 1821; a synagogue operated by 1862, and an 1883 school came under Alliance Israelite Universelle patronage in 1897, with a new building in 1911. Bulgarian-taught Zionist ideas spread as population grew to 950 by 1913. Following Greek annexation in 1919, the well-organized community (over 1,000) built a new synagogue, school, and community center by 1924, though 1930s emigration followed. German occupation left Jews largely unmolested until May 4, 1943, when men were arrested in the synagogue and ordered to gather their families for transfer to Poland; postwar restitution of community property and buildings largely failed. The community was formally dismantled in 1967, with only four Jews remaining by 1983. This cemetery's exact founding is unknown but presumed to date to the 14th century.
